newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Intl Network signals turn in IPO market.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Intl Network signals turn in IPO market.

text.p: International Network Services' strong market debut on Wednesday jolted the U.S. initial public offering market out of its summer lethargy and is a harbinger of several strong deals in the pipeline.

International Network, which provides services for complex enterprise networks, surged 92 percent, up 14-3/4 to 30-3/4 in early afternoon, topping the percent gainers on the Nasdaq and sending IPO analysts cheering.
"We're back, and we're back big. We have some good quality deals coming and the 'mad crowd' of momentum players are back and ready to play," said Manish Shah of the IPO Maven.
It was the first big hit since the IPO's market summer hiatus, which followed a downturn in the broader stock market coupled with a traditionally slow period.
"It's the best of all worlds from a technical point of view," said Richard Smith, managing syndicate director at Montgomery Securities.

"We've had a terrific flip-flop in the market from pretty negative to pretty positive and a large buildup of cash with eight weeks and nothing to buy. So it's a pretty interesting disequilibrium with a lot of cash looking for something to do," he said.

However, Smith said the market would probably still show some restraint. "I'm still not convinced that some of these concept-type companies, which should be in the earlier stage of venture capital, are going to be able to get done."

Shares of International Network priced at $16 each, above their estimated pricing range of $12-$14 -- which had been revised higher from an initial estimated range of $9-$11. The company offered 2.5 million shares.

Shah said he expects more hot deals coming soon, including computer reseller giant Ingram Micro Inc IM.N, Univision Communications Inc, Applied Analytical Industries Inc, retailer Abercrombie & Fitch Co, Houston Exploration Co, Dover Downs Entertainment Inc, and Advanced Fibre Communications Inc.
"They should all rise 30 to 35 percent minimum in the first six months, and Applied Analytical should double," said Shah.
